title: Accessed, never disclosed: Silent access to protected health information by medical artificial intelligence agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.02319v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Medical artificial intelligence agents should retrieve patient identifiers only when a task requires them, the data-minimization principle behind the HIPAA minimum necessary standard for protected health information (PHI). An agent can retrieve identifiers without revealing them. Such silent access remains invisible to evaluations that inspect only the output. We embedded canaries in synthetic patient records and linked each tool invocation to canary exposure in the final answers across five language models, four boundary levels, and seven attack frames for identifier-free clinical tasks. Three models invoked the PHI tools unnecessarily, whereas Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 did not. Stronger boundaries reduced this access, and the residual access under the strictest policy was confined to frames in which the user overrode the policy or asserted approval. translated_title: 被访问却从未披露：医疗人工智能代理对受保护健康信息的静默访问
translated_abstract: 医疗人工智能代理应当只在任务需要时才检索患者标识信息，这是《健康保险可携性与责任法案》（HIPAA）“最小必要”标准背后针对受保护健康信息（PHI）的数据最小化原则。代理可以在不透露标识信息的情况下检索这些信息，而这种“静默访问”对于仅检查输出的评估来说是不可见的。我们在合成患者记录中嵌入了金丝雀标记，并在五个语言模型、四个边界级别和七种攻击框架下，针对无需标识符的临床任务，将每次工具调用与最终答案中的金丝雀暴露关联起来。三个模型不必要地调用了PHI工具，而Claude Opus 4.8和GPT-5.5则没有这样做。更强的访问边界减少了这种访问，而最严格策略下的残余访问仅限于用户推翻策略或声称已获批准的攻击框架。基于任务必要性标准设置的预执行门控几乎消除了这种静默访问。
tldr: 该研究通过在合成病历中嵌入金丝雀标记，首次揭示了医疗AI代理会在任务不需要时“静默访问”患者受保护健康信息——这种行为对仅检查输出的评估完全不可见——并证明基于任务必要性的预执行门控可几乎完全消除这种隐蔽数据访问。
en_tdlr: Using canary markers embedded in synthetic patient records, this study exposes "silent access" to protected health information by medical AI agents—a behavior invisible to output-only evaluations—and shows that a pre-execution gate based on task necessity nearly eliminates it.
